newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine denies U.S. report it sold missiles to Libya.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine denies U.S. report it sold missiles to Libya.

text.p: Ukraine on Tuesday denied a U.S. newspaper report that Kiev had agreed to sell ballistic missiles to Libya in contravention of a U.N. arms embargo against the Arab state.

Deputy Foreign Minister Kostyantyn Hryshchenko called a late-evening news briefing to dismiss the allegation and to criticise the U.S. administration for failing to quash the reports in Monday and Tuesday editions of the Washington Times.
The newspaper quoted a Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) report as saying Ukraine had concluded a deal to sell short-range ballistic missiles to Libya and to service its Russian-built submarines.
It also quoted U.S. officials as expressing concern at the thought of any country trading arms with Libya.
"They (Washington) should state clearly that Ukraine is in no way guilty of such accusations. If there are some problems or questions, we would like to receive them officially," said Hryshchenko.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Yuri Sergeyev told an earlier news briefing the allegations were groundless and said someone was trying to discredit Ukraine as a member-state of the United Nations.
"The aim is also to create tension in Ukrainian-American relations or even to destroy the Ukraine-U.S. strategic partnership," Sergeyev said. "No such agreements were planned or have been planned."

The two countries have established a "strategic partnership" and Ukraine is the most active participant in NATO's Partnership for Peace programme as well as the third biggest recipient of U.S. foreign aid, he said.
Deputy minister Hryshchenko also suggested that the accusation played into the hands of Russia, which unlike Ukraine steadfastly opposes NATO expansion eastwards.

He showed reporters a photocopy of an article in an evening edition of Moscow's Izvestia daily with a photograph of President Leonid Kuchma and Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi side-by-side beneath the headline: "Has Ukraine gone over the top?" which also means "Has Ukraine hit the target?" in Russian.
"It is very strange that such accusations have been picked up so quickly by Moscow," he said.

"We have a very reliable and serious system of export controls...Everything is well checked and there is no way arms, military equipment or dual purpose goods could get through, wherever they are headed for," he added.
He said the report could be put down to over-zealous journalism or attempts by "certain circles" to damage U.S.-Ukrainian relations.

The U.N. Security Council imposed sanctions against Tripoli for its failure to hand over two suspects in the 1988 bombing of a U.S. airliner over Scotland which killed 270 people and over a French UTA airliner over Niger in 1989 which claimed 171 lives.
Ukraine has said it wants to cooperate with Libya in oil extraction, prospecting, transport, education and health care but stressed it would not break any embargo.
